## Before you upgrade

- **This is a security release.** It fixes two high and several medium issues found in a review of 0.4.0 (see Security fixes). Upgrade every server, including Docker and Helm installs: the 0.4.0 image was built with a Go that had known flaws.
- **Searches that build very many values are refused.** A search whose `eval` or `stats` makes more multivalue values than the search's memory allows now stops with an error that names the limit, instead of running the server out of memory. (RT-203)
- **More commands read past the newest 100 events.** A subsearch used as a filter, `map`, `addcoltotals`, `addtotals col`, `uniq`, `reverse`, `accum`, `transpose`, `untable`, `xyseries`, `return` and a `timechart` after other commands now read up to **Events per search** (Settings > Search) and are marked Sampled when more match. A subsearch that returns more than 1,000 distinct values now stops with an error instead of quietly using only some of them. Saved searches and dashboards using these may show different numbers. (SRCH-203)
- **osquery on a computer with its own key must enroll with that key.** A computer that sends osquery or OpenTelemetry data with only the line's token can no longer update the Endpoints row of a computer that has its own key. (ING-202, RT-201)
- **Response actions ask for your password again.** Running a response action or approving a playbook step now needs the password, code or passkey entered in the last 5 minutes; otherwise the page asks for it, and people who use single sign-on sign in again. (AUTH-207)
- **API tokens use only listed read requests.** A request made with an API token is allowed only if it is on a list of reads checked to change nothing; anything else gets `403 API tokens can only read`, even a `GET`. See [AI tools](https://signalith.io/docs/ai-tools/). (AUTH-212)
- **`signalith init -admin-password` is deprecated.** It puts the password on the command line, where other users of the computer can see it. Set `SIGNALITH_NEW_PASSWORD` instead. (DEP-205)
- **Agents update themselves.** Agent programs from 0.4.0 trust the same release key, so they move to 0.4.1 on their own once the server is upgraded. Agents still on 0.3.x need the install line from **Add data** run again, as for 0.4.0.

## Security fixes

- **OpenTelemetry requests can no longer grow into huge batches.** A scope name or a computer name in an OTLP request was copied to every event without being counted, so a request of about 1.5 KB could turn into about 100 GB of events and use up the server's memory. The scope name and `service.name` are now kept to 256 bytes and `host.name` to 255, and all of them count toward the request's 64 MB limit. (ING-201)
- **Searches are charged for the memory multivalue fields really use.** A 20 KB search could make the server hold about 3.8 GB, and a few at once could stop it; on a public demo no account was needed. Each value now counts at its real cost, and a search that would build too many is refused with an error naming the limit. (RT-203)
- **A line's token can no longer move another computer's Endpoints row.** A computer with its own key could have its last-seen time and address changed by any token through the OpenTelemetry or HEC intake, which kept its "agent silent" alert from firing. The check now uses the computer name taken from the events, and osquery on a computer with its own key must enroll with that key. (ING-202, RT-201)
- **Anonymous single sign-on failures no longer flood the audit log.** Anyone could write unlimited audit records through the single sign-on links, which could push real records out before the audit alerts read them. With single sign-on off they are not recorded, and otherwise they are rate-limited per address. (AUTH-201, RT-202, SRCH-201)
- **Renaming the built-in admin on a cluster keeps it turned off.** A rename with `signalith cluster apply` turned a turned-off built-in admin back on and dropped its two-step sign-in and passkeys. Both are now kept. Changes to the built-in admin from the command line on a cluster are now recorded in the audit log. (AUTH-202, AUTH-204)
- **The sign-in notice can't be skipped through a single sign-on link.** A link to the single sign-on start that claimed agreement skipped the notice. Agreement now counts only when it comes from the sign-in page, and the log records what was checked. (AUTH-205)
- **Built with a fixed Go.** Every download and the container image are built with Go 1.26.11, which fixes GO-2026-6859 (an HTTP/1 server crash). The 0.4.0 image was built with Go 1.27.1, which missed 16 standard-library fixes; the image now uses the same Go as the other downloads, pinned by digest. (CI-201, CI-202)

## What's new

- **Signed-in sessions.** Everyone can see their signed-in sessions in the account menu and end any of them, and admins can sign a user out everywhere from the Users page. A new setting, **Offer Keep me signed in** (`auth.keep_signed_in`), takes **Keep me signed in** away. (AUTH-206, AUTH-208, AUTH-210)
- **Audit alerts.** Admins can be told about Signalith's own audit records: built-in admin and admin sign-ins, lockouts, failed sign-ins, changes to users, tenants, tokens and settings, deletions, and lost or tampered audit records. Each alert is off until an admin turns it on and picks channels on the Notifications page. See [Notifications](https://signalith.io/docs/notifications/).
- **Sign-in notice.** Admins can show a notice on the sign-in page (a system use notification, NIST SP 800-53 AC-8), with an optional "I agree" box that the server checks for every sign-in. See [Sign-in notice](https://signalith.io/docs/sign-in-notice/).
- **Content refresh.** 2,642 SigmaHQ rules and 1,337 from Splunk security content, and the Entra ID `modifiedProperties` old value is mapped.

## Fixes

- Case task changes, storyline reads and evidence exports are recorded in the audit log, and case, report, template, playbook and response records name the action and the address. Case owners must be known users. (SRCH-214 to SRCH-222)
- Compliance: due times run from when a finding was raised, detection evidence needs a recent successful run, and history records keep who attested and chain to the one before. (SRCH-216, SRCH-220, SRCH-221)
- Behavior baselines: first-seen messages state their window, a program new to every computer raises once, and the bulk hour's neighbours are judged correctly. (SRCH-224 to SRCH-227)
- Audit alerts are read most urgent first, dropped records are shown on the Health page, late records are read again, and turning the alerts off or moving their channel sends a last message to the old one. (SRCH-202, SRCH-204 to SRCH-206, AUTH-203)
- Ingest: the agent's Fluent Bit check requires host name checking when no private CA is set; secrets are masked more widely and a blank value no longer crashes masking; the sender behind a trusted proxy is the real client; a stalled OTLP batch is answered 503 so the Collector retries; HEC accepts millisecond times and refuses NaN; a time written without a zone is no longer read as UTC: the event takes the collector's or arrival time and keeps the written time in its own field; one sender can no longer use up a day's new field names. (ING-207 to ING-214, ING-216 to ING-219)
- A locked address still lets in accounts that signed in from it before. (AUTH-213)
- The Docker cluster example uses HAProxy 3.1.
- auditd lines with a record type over 64 characters are kept as plain lines, which fixes a crash the nightly fuzz test found. (CI-204)
- The Docker quick start's `load-security.sh` no longer removes the snapshot role's mapping when it cannot reach OpenSearch. (DEP-202)
- Raising the summary days so the range reached back into last month no longer deletes last month's summaries.
- `[* inputlookup owners]` in a subsearch searches for the word again instead of failing.
- The Settings tab row has arrow buttons and wheel scrolling in a narrow window.
- A stylesheet block left open no longer limits the Metrics tab and chat dialogs to narrow screens.
- The package repositories show a page at `/apt/` and `/rpm/` instead of an error, and search engines are told not to follow the sign-in page's hidden single sign-on links.
- The security policy names 0.4 as the supported version.
